solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tot's initial reprimand for crying

indicators.note: initial asks for only the opening letter of the word Tot's

parts.note: an earful is a scolding, a reprimand

explanation.surface: A small child bursts into tears after being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is weeping or close to it, so the adjective matches crying used descriptively.

clue.text: Grab food and beer, heading off

parts.note: tack is food, as in hardtack, the ship's biscuit

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Seize something to eat and a drink, then leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle is to seize or grab, as a rugby player grabs an opponent.

clue.text: Poor sap treated suitably

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An unfortunate fool given the care he deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means fittingly or opportunely, relevant to the occasion.

clue.text: Order gal to feel pulse

indicators.note: order as a command to arrange these letters in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A doctor instructing a girl to take someone's pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse looks like a heartbeat; here it means an edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small pale bean, and beans, peas and lentils are pulses.

clue.text: Feline couplings can be heard

indicators.note: can be heard means the word is recognised by its sound when spoken

parts.note: links are couplings, connections

explanation.surface: Cats mating noisily enough to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears, a member of the feline family.

clue.text: Blimps regularly track aircraft

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of Blimps, starting with the first

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track or path

explanation.surface: Airships are being followed across the sky by some other flying machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is a type of aircraft with two sets of wings, one above the other.

clue.text: Make revolting violet-coloured biscuit

parts.note: a brand is a make of product

indicators.note: revolting in the sense of turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pansy is a purple-violet shade, named after the flower

explanation.surface: Producing a disgusting purple cookie.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a thin crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream.

clue.text: Maud sheds clothes after endless lager and spicy rice

indicators.note: after places the letters from Maud behind those from lager
endless cuts the final letter off the word for lager

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager

indicators.note: sheds clothes strips the outside letters of Maud, leaving her core

explanation.surface: Maud undresses after a beer and a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, a dish from South Asia and the Middle East.

clue.text: Answer four consecutive letters about a new currency

indicators.note: about means these letters go around the next pieces

parts.note: F, G, H and I follow one another in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle reply spelling out a run of letters that names some money.
explanation.walkthrough: Four consecutive letters could be any run; the crossers and the answer pin it to F, G, H, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the monetary unit of Afghanistan.

clue.text: Without leaders we might see an age of maturity

indicators.note: without leaders drops the first letter of each of the words we might see an

explanation.surface: Musing on when someone might reach adulthood if nobody guided them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is the age of majority in many countries, when a person legally becomes an adult.

clue.text: Brief all guards in Washington, first line of defence

parts.note: curt means brief, short in speech

indicators.note: guards means the word all surrounds and protects the following pieces

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A short instruction that everyone protecting the US capital is the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain wall is the outer defensive wall of a castle, the first barrier attackers meet.

clue.text: Stop someone telling joke

definitions.meaning: to silence someone, preventing them from speaking out, as with a cloth over the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Gag is both a verb for silencing a person and a noun for a joke.

clue.text: Ran out of drink and cursed, half-cut

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue

indicators.note: half-cut asks for only the back half of the word cursed

explanation.surface: Someone finished their drink, swore, and is a bit tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which suits the drinking surface; here it takes the last half of cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription or policy that has lapsed has expired, come to an end.

clue.text: Officer pulling wings off lady beetle and termite

indicators.note: wings off strips the outer letters from either side of the word lady

parts.note: to beetle is to overhang or project, as beetling brows jut out
termites are known as white ants

explanation.surface: A cruel child tearing the wings off insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady beetle and termite look like two insects, but beetle is the verb meaning stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer who assists a commanding officer with administration.

clue.text: Pretty good routine that holds attractions

parts.note: fair means pretty, good-looking
a round is a regular routine, as a postman's round

explanation.surface: A rather nice regime that has its appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is a site where rides, sideshows and other amusements are set up.

clue.text: Volatile vet is fearless and forceful

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, liable to change, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpredictable animal doctor who knows no fear and pushes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-assertive person states their views confidently and pushes for what they want, which is a forceful manner.

clue.text: Restore control over country

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts this piece above the next

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
a state is a country

explanation.surface: Bringing back authority over a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back into a former position, which is to restore.

clue.text: Mostly working with university, in one's element

indicators.note: mostly takes all but the last letter of the word for working

parts.note: acting means working, serving temporarily

indicators.note: in puts the university letter inside the contraction for one's

parts.note: I'm is one is, read as one's

explanation.surface: Busy at college and thoroughly at home there.
explanation.walkthrough: In one's element looks like an idiom for comfort; element is the definition, a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinium is a radioactive chemical element, number 89.

clue.text: Anxiety about millions leaving huge country

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for millions departs from the phrase

parts.note: a monster nation is a huge country
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Worry that large sums are draining out of a vast nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is a feeling of dismay and alarm, a close synonym of anxiety.

clue.text: Winds up unnecessary contracts

indicators.note: contracts means shrinks, so the word for unnecessary loses its final letter

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: A business closing down pointless agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: Winds up suggests ending; here it is British slang for teases.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them, and to wind someone up is the same.

clue.text: Advancing relatives turn up gaping and twitching

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: open means gaping
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: Relatives arriving with mouths open and faces twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotic describes nepotism, favouring family members by promoting them.

clue.text: Greener gym conserves power

indicators.note: conserves means keeps safe within, so the letters sit inside Greener gym

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly fitness centre saves electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy and power are both terms for the capacity to do work.

clue.text: Oddly neglected fiances kiss saucy amateur

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of fiances are ignored, leaving the even ones

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss
pert means cheeky, saucy

explanation.surface: Engaged couples, forgotten, share a cheeky kiss like novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, as an amateur or novice does.

clue.text: Dads ultimately get some stick

parts.note: pa is father, so pas are dads

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of each of the words get and some

explanation.surface: Fathers end up taking criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Get some stick is a British idiom for being criticised; stick is the definition, glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste is to stick something with adhesive.

clue.text: Quiet old man hiding in an under-fire vessel

indicators.note: hiding in puts the next pieces out of sight within the word an

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
old man is slang for father, pa

explanation.surface: A silent elderly man concealing himself in a ship that is being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: Under-fire suggests attack; it means a tray beneath a grate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash-pan is a receptacle placed beneath a fire grate to catch the ash.

clue.text: Tea party excluding Bohemian fellow

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: excluding means the word for Bohemian is left out of party

parts.note: arty means bohemian, artistically unconventional

explanation.surface: A tea party that shuts out the unconventional bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man, a fellow.

clue.text: Badly want to lose weight

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for weight must drop out

parts.note: will means desire or want

explanation.surface: A dieter who is desperate to slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can be an adverb meaning poorly, as in ill-treated, so it matches badly.

clue.text: Father got us bananas, much in demand

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Dad bought us fruit that everyone wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sought-after is desired by many people, popular and hard to get.

clue.text: Man perhaps stops crazy fool

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so this piece fills the inside of the word for crazy

parts.note: mad means crazy
the Isle of Man is one example of an isle

explanation.surface: Some fellow puts an end to a mad jester's antics.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to deceive or lead them astray, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Sanctimonious, before experiencing pain

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
achy means suffering an ache

explanation.surface: Smug and self-righteous until the hurting started.
explanation.definitionFit: A preachy person moralises in a self-righteous way, like someone sanctimonious.
